addedLines: - claude: Catch-all for any task that doesn't fit a more specific agent. FleetView's default when no agent name is typed. (Tools: *)

- Explore: Read-only search agent for broad fan-out searches — when answering means sweeping many files, directories, or naming conventions and you only need the conclusion, not the file dumps. It reads excerpts rather than whole files, so it locates code; it doesn't review or audit it. Specify search breadth: "medium" for moderate exploration, "very thorough" for multiple locations and naming conventions. - general-purpose: General-purpose agent for researching complex questions, searching for code, and executing multi-step tasks. When you are searching for a keyword or file and are not confident that you will find the right match in the first few tries use this agent to perform the search for you. (Tools: *)

- Plan: Software architect agent for designing implementation plans. Use this when you need to plan the implementation strategy for a task. - dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.

- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo, defaults to 10m) - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). - claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.

content.text:
q29.

**`web/src/connect.ts`; JWT access token (in-memory + localStorage, `Authorization: Bearer`) + refresh token (HttpOnly `memos_refresh` cookie), with Personal Access Tokens as the programmatic alternative; `server/auth`**

**Frontend interceptor — `web/src/connect.ts:156`**
- `authInterceptor` is attached to the Connect-RPC transport (`web/src/connect.ts:184-189`) that backs every service client (memo, user, attachment, AI, etc.). The transport uses `fetch` with `credentials: "include"` (`connect.ts:57`) so the refresh cookie rides along.
- Per request it calls `getRequestToken()` (`connect.ts:124`) and sets `Authorization: Bearer <token>`. That does a *preflight* refresh when the access token is within 30s of expiry (`REQUEST_TOKEN_EXPIRY_BUFFER_MS`), and *reactively* on a `Code.Unauthenticated` response it refreshes once, marks the retry with an `X-Retry` header, and replays; if the refresh fails it calls `redirectOnAuthFailure()` (`connect.ts:161-177`).
- Refresh goes through a separate transport with no interceptors to avoid recursion (`connect.ts:64-72`) calling `AuthService.RefreshToken`, and is deduped by `tokenRefreshManager` (`connect.ts:30-51`, `89`).

**Token storage — `web/src/auth-state.ts`**
- Access token + expiry kept in module memory and mirrored to `localStorage` under `memos_access_token` / `memos_token_expires_at`; a `BroadcastChannel` (`memos_token_sync`) shares freshly refreshed tokens between tabs. `web/src/hooks/useTokenRefreshOnFocus.ts` refreshes proactively on tab focus using a larger 2-minute buffer.
- The refresh token itself is never in JS — it's a server-set cookie.

**Backend validation — `server/auth/`**
- `server/auth/token.go` defines the token model: access tokens (JWT, 15 min, audience `user.access-token`), refresh tokens (JWT, 30 days, cookie `memos_refresh`), and PATs (prefix `memos_pat_`).
- `server/auth/authenticator.go` — `Authenticator.Authenticate` / `AuthenticateToUser` extract the bearer token (`server/auth/extract.go`), validate access tokens statelessly by signature (`AuthenticateByAccessTokenV2`), route `memos_pat_`-prefixed tokens to `AuthenticateByPAT` (recording last-used asynchronously), and fall back to the refresh cookie, which *is* checked against the DB for revocation (`AuthenticateByRefreshToken`).
- Consumers: `server/router/api/v1/connect_interceptors.go:222`, plus `server/router/api/v1/authz.go`, `sse_handler.go`, and `server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go`.
